review.method: Acceptance suite run locally with `retail,gpu,audio` (CS_GAME_DIR, CS_CAPABILITIES): the two ignored tests ran — the retail test read the installation's own GLOBALS.SCRIPT (six `sound` declarations in order mouseclick, mouseover, mouseclick, mouseover, entertext, entertext_error, and the @ctl@SK music control given music_splash.wav) and decoded every member they name with the production decoder (ASSETS/SOUNDS/*.WAV of crimson.rof; the music is a stereo 22 050 Hz track over thirty seconds long), and the windowed test drove `cs --cs-path $CS_GAME_DIR --front-end --smoke-seconds 14 --capture-dir private/evidence/FE-MENU-4` on this machine's GPU and default audio output (Apple M3 Pro, Metal): report.json records the music loop started and the scripted pointer and typing produced rollover, press and text-entry cues with no refusal from the output, beside the framebuffer PNGs. The synthetic tests prove the script reading, the bus/loop/one-shot shape of each device command, refusals by code and the presenter's triggers over a recording device. The audio claim stops at the source boundary: the device was asked to play the members and accepted every command; no person listened (`human_review` is the owner's) and no speaker capture exists. The run is scripted, never `human_play`, and no original executable ran. LIMITS: see the overrides. Validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass.
